question: Has any government or central bank issued a CBDC or other public-sector asset on Stellar?

golden.answer: As of 2026-11-14 no central bank has launched a production CBDC on Stellar. Ukraine's electronic hryvnia pilot (December 2021) was e-money issued by the commercial bank TASCOMBANK with Bitt; the National Bank of Ukraine said it was not its e-hryvnia. One government issues directly: the Marshall Islands' USDM1 sovereign bond has paid universal basic income on Stellar since December 2025.
keyFacts: Ukraine's electronic hryvnia pilot on Stellar was run by TASCOMBANK and Bitt.
The National Bank of Ukraine said that pilot was not its e-hryvnia CBDC.
The Marshall Islands issued its USDM1 sovereign bond on Stellar.
avoid: Do NOT say the National Bank of Ukraine issued a CBDC on Stellar.
golden.notes: An answer that names a production CBDC on Stellar needs a dated primary source; none was found on 2026-11-14. Tokenized government debt from private issuers such as Etherfuse is not a government issuance. Other sourced public-sector programs may be named and are not required.

truth.notes: The negative claim is dated and source-relative: absence from SDF's CBDC pages plus one web sweep. Re-run the sweep at reverifyBy.

No central bank CBDC had reached production on the Stellar public network as of November 2026.

corroboration.claim: Ukraine's electronic hryvnia pilot on Stellar was launched in December 2021 (announced 2021-12-14) by TASCOMBANK and Bitt.

evidence.note: SDF press release: Bitt and TASCOMBANK "have launched a pilot project to issue an electronic hryvnia on Stellar".
Bitt's copy of the release carries the dateline December 14, 2021.
NBU news dated 15 Dec 2021 names the Ministry of Digital Transformation, TASCOMBANK, Bitt and the Stellar Development Foundation.

corroboration.claim: The National Bank of Ukraine stated the pilot was not an issue of its e-hryvnia CBDC; a commercial bank issued electronic money.

evidence.note: Deputy Governor Oleksii Shaban: "This pilot project is not directly concerned with issuing the e-hryvnia, the NBU’s digital currency. Under new legislation, the NBU is the only authority that can issue the e-hryvnia."
"This regulated electronic hryvnia will be built under the current e-money legislation of Ukraine."

corroboration.claim: The Republic of the Marshall Islands issued the USDM1 sovereign bond, and its universal basic income payments in USDM1 run on Stellar from December 2025.

evidence.note: Ministry of Finance: USDM1 is "issued by the Republic of the Marshall Islands", backed 1:1 by short-dated U.S. Treasury instruments.
Ministry whitepaper: "Transfers occur on the Stellar blockchain."
SDF press release title names the first on-chain UBI disbursement on Stellar via the digital sovereign bond USDM1.
CoinDesk, 2025-12-16: Marshall Islands launches blockchain-based UBI on Stellar with USDM1.

corroboration.claim: As of 2026-11-14 no central bank had launched a production CBDC on Stellar.

evidence.note: The only CBDC-labelled Stellar project found is the Ukrainian pilot, which the central bank says is not its CBDC.
Web sweep returned no production CBDC on Stellar; it listed the Ukrainian pilot and the Marshall Islands bond, and wrongly attributed the pilot to the NBU.
Page text extracted 2026-11-14 offers a CBDC whitepaper and names no launched central bank currency.

corroboration.claim: The National Bank of Ukraine issued a CBDC on Stellar.

evidence.note: "the term e-hryvnia only refers to an NBU-issued CBDC"; the Stellar pilot had a commercial bank issue electronic money.

evidence: Sibling sweep: q-hist-unhcr-stellar-aid-assist (UN aid payments) and q-rwa-projects-tokenizing-stellar (RWA issuers) agree; no battery case states the Ukrainian pilot or USDM1.
